scope_plain: Every Orange County voter, including all of Orlando. Nonpartisan, so no party labels on the ballot. This is the runoff between the top two finishers from the Aug 18 primary.
office_explainer: Runs county government day to day and chairs the County Commission: budget, roads, growth, transit.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Mayor Jerry Demings is term-limited. Orange County's strong mayor manages about 8,000 county employees and a multibillion-dollar budget, and speaks for the county on transportation, airport and tourism boards.

candidates.name: Chris Messina
candidates.background: Winter Park tech entrepreneur with a Harvard MBA, a registered Republican making his second run for mayor (he also ran in 2022). Vice chair of Orange County Watch, 2022 to 2025. Finished second on Aug 18 with 27.1%.

own_words.text: "Low median wages stifle economic opportunity for many Orange County citizens."
"We need to get rid of waste, fraud & bureaucracy in County government."
On Amendment 3: "I will vote Yes to lower property taxes by increasing the Homestead exemption."

candidates.name: Tiffany Moore Russell
candidates.background: Orange County Clerk of Courts for more than 12 years, and a county commissioner for eight years before that (District 6, first won in 2006). A registered Democrat. Finished first on Aug 18 with 32.0%.

own_words.text: "I will expand workforce and affordable housing through public-private partnerships."
"Orange County needs a dedicated funding source to address a multi-modal transportation plan for the future."
On Amendment 3: "I would vote No on the constitutional amendment to reduce property taxes."

scope_plain: Every voter in Orange and Osceola counties, including all of Orlando. Nonpartisan runoff between the top two from Aug 18.

From his campaign site: "I believe the courtroom belongs to the public."
